lines.text: On the first Sunday of every month, a community hall in Tampines turns
into a workshop. Volunteers sit behind long tables and waits to repair
lines.note: Agreement: 'Volunteers' is plural, so 'sit … and wait'.

lines.text: broken fans, kettles and toys that residents bring in. Nothing is threw

lines.text: away until someone has tried to fix it. Most of the volunteers are retired
technicians, but a few are students who simply enjoy take things apart.
Each repair is free, and visitors are encouraged to stay and watch how
the work is done. Mr Lim, which started the sessions, says the aim is not

lines.text: only to save money. He wants people to think careful before they replace

lines.text: volunteers kept more than two thousand item out of the rubbish bin.
Many visitors leave with a working appliance and an new skill as well.
lines.note: Article: 'new' starts with a consonant sound, so it is 'a new skill'.

lines.text: For Mr Lim, that second gift matters more than the first one does.
